speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your severe abdominal pain in more detail: where is it located, does it radiate anywhere, and on a scale of 1 to 10, how intense is it? Additionally, you mentioned nausea, vomiting, and dysuria; please tell me how long these symptoms have been occurring.

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old female. The patient presents with a 5-day history of severe abdominal pain and cramping, accompanied by nausea and vomiting. She reports pain with urination and also experienced burning pain during sexual intercourse 3 days ago. She mentions being sexually active with one male partner, using condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID).

Based on your age, sexual activity with inconsistent condom use, dysuria, and the specific history of pain during intercourse (dyspareunia) alongside lower abdominal pain and nausea, you have classic signs of an upper genital tract infection. This is a medical emergency that requires immediate treatment to prevent infertility. I will order tests to confirm the diagnosis and identify the causative organism.

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis, Urine Culture, Complete Blood Count (CBC), and Pelvic Ultrasound.
REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic Ultrasound.
